questions.implements: Does the diff implement what the repository records for the Jira issue, and add or change a test that checks it? Judge the code in the diff, not the answer.

judge.reason: Yes. The diff makes all three behaviors the item asks for. placeOrder takes an optional note. It counts the note in code points and throws NoteTooLongError if the note has more than 200, before it prices, reserves stock, or charges, so no order is placed. The returned Order also keeps the note. Two new tests are tagged @req R-ORDER-NOTE. The first checks that a 200-character note is kept on the order, and that a missing note is stored as an empty string. The second checks that a 201-character note is rejected with NoteTooLongError, that stock stays at 5 and that the audit log has no entries, which shows no order went through. Counting code points is a fair reading of "characters", and the boundary cases at 200 and 201 are both tested.

finalMessage:
SHOP-62 is implemented as the trace item `R-ORDER-NOTE`. All 38 tests pass (36 existing, 2 new). I did not commit.

**What changed**
- `src/checkout.ts`: `placeOrder` takes an optional `note` argument (defaults to `""`, so existing callers are unaffected). A note longer than `NOTE_MAX_CHARS` (200) throws `NoteTooLongError` before anything is priced, reserved, or charged. `Order` gained a `note` field, which the placed order keeps.
- `src/checkout.test.ts`: two tests tagged `@req R-ORDER-NOTE`. One checks that a 200-character note is kept and that an omitted note is stored as `""`. The other checks that a 201-character note is rejected, with stock still at 5 and no audit entries.

**Choices I made**
- "Characters" means Unicode code points, so `[...note].length` is used. The boundary test uses 200 emoji, which are 400 UTF-16 units and are accepted.
- The note is stored exactly as given. I did not trim it.
- I did not add a new trace item. `R-ORDER-NOTE` (external `jira:SHOP-62`, revision 1) already states this behavior, so I linked the code and tests to it with `@req` comments, which is how this repo links code to items. `trace.yaml` is unchanged. I could not reach Jira directly, so the item text I worked from is the copy in `trace.yaml`.

**Items linked to the code I changed**
- `R-CHECKOUT-ORDER` (refines `N-BUY`), on `placeOrder`: still true. The note check happens before pricing, reserving, and charging, so the order of those steps is unchanged. Tested by "places an order".
- `R-CHECKOUT-SESSION` (refines `N-ACCOUNT-SAFE`), on `placeOrder`: still true. The session is still validated first. Tested by "needs a valid session".
- `R-ORDER-NOTE`: the item I implemented. It is true with this change. It has no `controls` or `refines` link to any risk or threat.

**Risk or threat items touched:** none. None of the items above control or refine `RISK-*` or `THREAT-*` items, so no review question arises from the trace. `R-CHARGE-AMOUNT`, `R-REFUND-LIMIT`, and `R-LOGIN-LOCKOUT` are not touched.

**Tests run:** `node --test` over the full suite, all passing. I also ran `src/checkout.test.ts` alone, 5 of 5 passing.
